Once cleared (typically week 6–7 of the programme), you can introduce:
- Dead bug (already in the plan)
- Bird dog (already in the plan)
- Side plank progressions (already in the plan)
- Pallof press (anti-rotation, safe for diastasis recti)
- Pelvic tilts (already in the plan)

Avoid until full clearance:
- Crunches, sit-ups, v-ups
- Planks (full front plank)
- Hollow holds
- Heavy compound lifts with Valsalva

The current programme emphasizes posterior chain, glute activation, and isometric core stability—which rebuild deep core function safely. Once her OB clears her, add pallof_press and progress plank variations in weeks 7–12.

HIIT is contraindicated until week 10–11 at earliest, and only after OB clearance at the six-week check-up.

**Why the delay:**
- High-impact jumping/plyometrics stress the pelvic floor and incision site
- Rapid breathing patterns can increase intra-abdominal pressure
- Risk of pelvic floor dysfunction and diastasis recti aggravation

**Safe progression:**
- **Weeks 1–8:** Walking only (low-impact steady-state cardio)
- **Weeks 9–10:** Can introduce low-impact intervals (walk/jog alternation on flat ground, no jumping)
- **Week 11–12:** If pelvic floor is strong and pain-free, consider very gentle HIIT with non-impact modalities:
  - Cycling intervals (stationary bike)
  - Rowing intervals
  - Battle ropes (if core is solid)

**Never add:**
- Jump rope
- Box jumps
- Burpees
- High-knees sprints
- Skater jumps
- Tuck jumps

If she wants conditioning intensity before week 11, use **tempo walking** (faster pace, longer duration) or **cycling intervals** instead. Always screen for pelvic floor symptoms (heaviness, leaking, pain) before progressing.
